questionText: Suppose two hosts are connected by a point-to-point link and they are configured to use Stop-and-Wait protocol for reliable data transfer. Identify in which one of the following scenarios, the utilization of the link is the lowest.
options: Longer link length and lower transmission rate
Longer link length and higher transmission rate
Shorter link length and lower transmission rate
Shorter link length and higher transmission rate
explanation:
Efficiency / Utilization ($\\eta$) of Stop-and-Wait Protocol:

The link utilization (efficiency) in Stop-and-Wait protocol is given by:
$$\\eta = \\frac{1}{1 + 2a}$$

where $a = \\frac{T_p}{T_t} = \\frac{\\text{Propagation Delay}}{\\text{Transmission Delay}}$.

We know that:
1. Propagation Delay ($T_p$) = $\\frac{\\text{Link Length } (d)}{\\text{Propagation Speed } (v)}$
2. Transmission Delay ($T_t$) = $\\frac{\\text{Packet Size } (L)}{\\text{Transmission Rate } (B)}$

Substituting $T_p$ and $T_t$ into $a$ gives:
$$a = \\frac{d \\cdot B}{v \\cdot L}$$

To achieve the lowest utilization ($\\eta$), the parameter $a$ must be maximized.
Since $a \\propto d \\cdot B$, $a$ is maximized when:
1. The link length ($d$) is longer.
2. The transmission rate ($B$) is higher.

Thus, lower utilization occurs with a longer link length and higher transmission rate.
